patients.summary: Remote software developer with mild ileocolonic Crohn's disease after a 2020 ileocecal resection, mild asthma and recurrent UTIs. Vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism (2022) and B12 deficiency anemia (2023), then a urethral diverticulum with three pyelonephritis episodes, the last complicated by ceftriaxone anaphylaxis in the ICU (2026); now referred to urology.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F here to establish. Moved to Easthampton this spring, works from home writing software. Previous PCP in NY.

Crohn's: ileocolonic, many years. Had a laparoscopic ileocecal resection in 2020 (appendix removed with it). Since then bowels mostly settled, 1-3 formed BMs/day, no blood. Sees an outside GI group yearly, not on any maintenance medicine; she says GI calls it mild.
Asthma: since childhood, uses albuterol maybe once a month, more with colds or cold air. No ED visits or steroids in years.
UTIs: bladder infections a couple of times a year for a long stretch. Also had UTIs early in a pregnancy a few years ago, treated with nitrofurantoin. Never a kidney infection.
Supplements: prenatal vitamin and ferrous sulfate daily, both from years back; she just keeps taking them.

PSH: lap ileocecal resection 2020.
Allergies: PCN (hives), sulfa (rash).
FHx: mother RA. Father asthma, seasonal allergies. Sister has Crohn's.
SH: never smoker, drinks once or twice a month, vegetarian. Mostly indoors at a desk; tries to walk on weekends.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. Vitals per flowsheet, BMI 22. HEENT unremarkable, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. No CVA tenderness. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Establishing care, health maintenance: Tdap today (last 2010). HIV and HCV screen, CMP, CBC, lipids. Pap 2019 normal in old records, next due 2022-2024 window - will do co-test at a future physical.
2. Crohn's, mild, post-resection: GI following. Will ask her to have them cc us.
3. Mild intermittent asthma: albuterol PRN, refills on file.
4. Hx recurrent UTIs: none recently. Call early for symptoms.
5. Supplements: continue as she takes them.
RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn.

documents.body: Karen - your blood work from Tuesday is all normal: blood counts, kidney and liver function, electrolytes, cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
Date of service: 05/10/2022

Dear Doctor,
I saw Ms. Duffy for her yearly review of ileocolonic Crohn's disease, about two years out from laparoscopic ileocecal resection. She reports one to three formed stools daily without bleeding, nocturnal stooling or abdominal pain. Weight is stable. Abdominal exam is benign.

Allergies: penicillin, sulfonamides.
Medications: albuterol as needed, prenatal multivitamin, ferrous sulfate.

Impression: Crohn's disease, clinically mild and quiet after resection. We will continue observation without maintenance therapy. I will see her in a year, sooner for symptoms.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

orders.reason: vitamin D 12 with elevated PTH, low calcium, bone pain

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33F annual. Main thing today: since around March she has felt progressively worn out, legs feel weak climbing stairs, and she aches deep in her shins, thighs and lower back. No injury. Sleeping fine, mood ok (PHQ-2 1). No fevers, weight steady. Bowels at baseline per her, GI saw her in May. Asthma quiet.

Works from home, rarely outside on weekdays. Vegetarian.

Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate.
Allergies: PCN (hives), sulfa (rash).

Exam: tired-appearing but comfortable. Vitals per flowsheet. Conjunctivae a touch pale. Thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mild tenderness pressing over both tibias, no swelling or deformity. Strength 5/5 but she says stairs are harder. Reflexes 2+ symmetric.

A/P
1. Fatigue, weakness, diffuse bone pain after ileal resection, indoor job, vegetarian - worried about vitamin D / bone mineral problem. CMP, phos, 25-OH vit D, PTH, CBC, TSH today.
2. Health maintenance: Pap due within the next couple of years, she'd rather do it next time. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit in October.
3. Crohn's, asthma: stable.
Will call with results.

documents.title: Results: vitamin D, calcium, PTH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vit D 12 (low), calcium 8.1 (low), PTH 88 (high), alk phos 120 (top of normal), phos 3.0. Fits vitamin D deficiency with a compensatory PTH rise, likely malabsorption after the ileal resection plus little sun. Hgb 11.6 with MCV 101 - mild, recheck once the vitamin D is sorted. TSH normal. Referring to endocrinology given the PTH and bone pain.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Karen, your vitamin D is quite low (12) and your calcium is a little low, which has pushed your parathyroid hormone up. That combination can absolutely cause the tiredness, weakness and bone aches you described. Your blood count is a bit low too; I'd like to recheck that after we treat the vitamin D. I've referred you to endocrinology so they can confirm the plan for replacing it. Their office will call you to schedule.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: That actually makes me feel better, at least there's a reason. Should I start vitamin D on my own while I wait?

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Their first opening is about 4 weeks out, and they'll likely want a high-dose course, so let's let them set it up. If the appointment slips past mid-September let me know.

conditions.label: Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to vitamin D deficiency

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule (50,000 units) by mouth once weekly for 8 weeks

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice
Date of service: 09/20/2022
Reason for referral: low vitamin D, elevated PTH

History: Ms. Duffy is a 33-year-old woman with ileocolonic Crohn's disease who had an ileal resection two years ago. Over about six months she has had increasing fatigue, proximal muscle weakness and aching bone pain, worst in the legs. She works remotely and is indoors most of the day. Diet vegetarian.

Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed, prenatal multivitamin daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Family history: mother rheumatoid arthritis, father asthma, sister Crohn's disease.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 78, BMI 22. She looks pale. Tender to palpation along both lower legs. No proximal muscle wasting. Thyroid not enlarged.

Data (referring office, 08/23/2022): calcium 8.1 mg/dL, phosphate 3.0 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 12 ng/mL, intact PTH 88 pg/mL.

Assessment: Secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D deficiency, most likely from reduced absorption after ileal resection and limited sun exposure. The low-normal phosphate and borderline alkaline phosphatase raise concern for early osteomalacia; repletion should address it.

Plan:
- Ergocalciferol 50,000 units once weekly for 8 weeks.
- Then cholecalciferol 2000 units daily, ongoing.
- Recheck calcium, 25-OH vitamin D and PTH with her PCP about 3 months from now. I am happy to see her again if PTH does not normalize.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid, bivalent COVID booster R deltoid. Pt on week 5 of weekly vitamin D, says legs already ache less. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule (2000 units) by mouth daily

documents.title: Done with the weekly vitamin D
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Took the last of the 8 weekly capsules on Sunday. Endo said to switch to 2000 units daily after. Can that go on my list here? I bought it OTC.

documents.title: RE: Done with the weekly vitamin D
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Added vitamin D3 2000 units daily to your medication list. You're due for the recheck labs early December; the PCP put in a follow-up for Dec 6.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: vitamin D deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished ergocalciferol 50k weekly x8 in mid-Nov, now on D3 2000 daily. Bone aches much better, legs stronger on stairs. But fatigue is the same or worse. Over the last few weeks: episodes of her heart racing for a minute or two, a few times a week, at rest; and her tongue has been sore and tender, hurts with spicy food. No chest pain, no syncope, no dyspnea beyond baseline. No melena or blood in stool, bowels at baseline. Still vegetarian, eats eggs and dairy rarely.

Exam: pale. HR regular today. Tongue smooth and reddened. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen benign. No edema.

A/P
1. Vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism: recheck vit D, PTH, calcium today. Continue D3 2000.
2. Fatigue, palpitations, glossitis, pallor, MCV 101 in August: concern for B12 deficiency after ileal resection plus vegetarian diet. CBC today; if anemia has progressed will refer to heme.
3. Palpitations: likely related; revisit once anemia addressed.

documents.title: Results 12/7
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vit D 32, PTH 54, Ca 9.0 - repleted, PTH normalized. Hgb now 9.8, MCV 105 - macrocytic anemia, worse than August. Hematology referral placed. Will call her.

documents.title: Call: results and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Vitamin D and parathyroid numbers are now normal. Blood count has dropped to 9.8 with large red cells; explained this points toward B12 or similar deficiency and that hematology can sort out the cause and the right replacement. Referral sent, she'll watch for their call. Advised ED for chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath at rest. She understands.
